hashRule: sha256 over canonical JSON of this file, exposed by cleanupCriteriaHash() in robustness.mjs and checked by verifyCleanupCriteria(); every plan 210 Task 5 manifest and report and the Task 6 decision record pin it, and assertCleanupCriteriaPin refuses drift

rulesFirst.decision: decision rules are pre-registered and committed before any Task 5 run
rulesFirst.reason: The 188.10 lesson: only pre-registered rules survive scrutiny. A rule changed after a Task 5 result is read is a new owner decision, not a revision of this file.

auditScope.decision: memory-observational, memory-fabric, memory-wiki and the parts of memory-core only they use; memory-rag and memory-compaction are excluded

postReleaseTrack.decision: the audit runs on the experimental line (plan 215); the stable surface it leaves graduates in Task 10

gapPredictions.rule: canonical hash of the `predictions` array only: Task 5 scores these predictions as frozen here. The `deferred` entries may record a measured disposition after the diagnostic leg; their protocol and rule text must stay equal to `preRegistered` below.

plan202Task5.note: v2 differs from v1 only in criteria.transport (gate 16, 2026-11-01); every rule is byte-identical. The full target, not the -screen variant, is carried: candidate-gap halving per suite and the ability guard as a veto.

partitions.rule: Every rule here uses development partitions only. Held-out partitions stay unread until plan 210 Task 9, so a removal needs no held-out confirmation: Task 9 accepts the product with the removals in it, and a removal that hurts shows up there as a miss.

statistics.method: paired cluster analysis of scripts/memory-bench/stats.mjs (clustered by source conversation, haystack or persona), every arm paired against its base on identical items
statistics.unit: points: percentage points of the target metric (accuracy, task success or W-row rate x 100); cost and latency are relative
statistics.answerModels: keep and fix-kept need the CI lower bound above 0 on at least one answer model and no answer model negative; removal non-inferiority must hold on every answer model

features.rule: Every ledger candidate receives exactly one verdict from these rules. Non-candidate ledger rows (accepted evidence) are not re-decided.

verdicts.computedBy: cleanupVerdict() in robustness.mjs, called by acceptance-report.mjs --plan 210; no hand-set value

when: CI upper bound < 0 on any ability of any suite on any answer model
negative.overrides: everything: a keep reason, a passing fix and an owner hold do not apply. Keeping a negative feature needs a new owner decision that changes this file, recorded before the Task 6 record is generated.

benefit.on: the feature's target metric from its gap-predictions entry
benefit.source: existing evidence (ledger status `benefit`) or a Task 5 arm

costOrLatency.on: the feature's own suite, measured as the paired mean of its leave-one-out arm
costOrLatency.rule: the cost or latency role counts only when accuracy stays within 2 points at the CI lower bound

plan202Task5.rule: These features carry plan 202 Task 5's deferred arms, scored by the pinned Task 5 rules (candidate-gap halving per suite, ability guard as a veto). Those rows are reported next to this file's verdict and never overridden by it: a Task 5 miss bars `keep` on benefit, so the feature is decided by fix-kept, removal or inconclusive, and Task 6 records the miss as a plan 202 Task 5 miss.

fixKept.appliesTo: a gap-predictions entry with verdict `fix-and-measure` whose change is not `as-is` (a real fix, not a plain ablation)
fixKept.when: the fix measured once meets its own prediction's direction and its CI lower bound on the predicted metric is above 0
fixKept.onMiss: the feature is decided by the other rules as shipped without the fix; the fix is deleted

remove.when: no keep reason, no fix kept, and removal is non-inferior on development partitions

workOutcome.source: work-outcome-criteria.json `work` row margins, applied with the feature removed against the configuration that has it

remove.inert: a feature in `inertRemoval.features` meets non-inferiority by the byte-identical-preset test instead of a paid arm

inconclusive.when: no keep reason, no fix kept, not negative, and removal non-inferiority is not shown (missing arm, missing stratum or the CI crosses the margin)
inconclusive.rule: An unmeasured mechanism never becomes an API-level-1 obligation. Task 6 lists it; the owner removes it or holds it in the experimental tier with a written reason.

ownerNegativeOverrides.reason: The only evidence is the memory-off arm, which turns off all of memory and so does not isolate lexical retrieval. Its overall effect is +26 to +60 points on every suite and model. The negative rule fired on a single 12-question LoCoMo `adversarial` stratum (small model), where answering without memory is expected to win. Removing the core search is not a candidate.
ownerNegativeOverrides.scope: waives only the per-ability CI trigger of the negative rule; a ledger `negative` status or a safety failure still removes the feature

experimentalTier.documentedIn: packages/memory/fabric/README.md `## Compatibility` (and the owning package's README for observational and wiki features)
experimentalTier.promise: outside the API-level-1 promise: an experimental feature can change or be removed in a minor version
experimentalTier.onlyRoute: the experimental tier is the only way to keep a feature without a keep or fix-kept verdict

inertRemoval.test: With the feature's code removed, the conversational and coding presets' provider requests and tool schemas are byte-identical on the offline replay fixtures (mock provider). A feature that any shipped preset or reference-host default turns on, or whose test is not byte-identical, needs a paid leave-one-out arm under C-1.

conditional.rule: no-credible-path rows that are active by default outside the presets (similar links are always available; widen and narrow run on the default lifecycle values). The byte-identical-preset test runs first; if it is not byte-identical, the removal needs a paid leave-one-out arm under C-1.

transferred.rule: These features are excluded from this plan's verdicts. Each gets the Task 6 verdict `transferred -> plan NNN`, and that plan writes its final disposition. None of them is removed, kept or fixed here, and none is scored as a miss.

closure.rule: Waves 2 and 3 of gate C-1 are cancelled and no job of theirs runs. The report reads wave 1 only and reports a cancelled arm as `cancelled` and a transferred row as `transferred`, never as a miss.

amendments.text: Added `transferred` and `closure`, and removed the transferred rows from `inertRemoval`. No rule, threshold or verdict precedence changed for any remaining feature.

amendments.by: owner (Task 6 review of the wave-1 report)
amendments.text: Added `ownerNegativeOverrides` (retrieval.lexical) after the wave-1 report was read, as the negative rule requires: keeping a negative feature is a new owner decision that changes this file. No other rule, threshold or verdict precedence changed.

f4DiagnosticLeg.protocol: Task 5 diagnostic leg under C-1, pre-registered in Task 4: per suite x model (beam-100k/dev, locomo/dev, longmemeval-m/dev), run the best read-time arm (gather + expansion + card excerpt + grouping) and the oracle arm on the same questions with validated ingestion. A failure counts toward extraction only if the oracle answers it, the read-time arm does not, the report's evidenceCounts show the gold evidence was delivered or was a candidate, the ability is state or aggregation, and the failure id is unique (repeats collapsed). Source and protocol hashes are pinned.
f4DiagnosticLeg.rule: complete attribution and < 5% -> not-needed (F4's remedy closed; the existing extractor is not thereby declared reliable); >= 5% irrecoverable in any suite x model -> fix-and-measure, the original scoped Task 17 remedy (opt-in `conversational-facts`); incomplete attribution -> stays unmeasured and no preset is built. Task 13's >= 5% shared-entity/not-in-query condition is kept separately; no graph store.
f4DiagnosticLeg.originalBars: plan 202 Task 17 acceptance as written: exchange citations, scope and consent inheritance, unchanged `conversational`, <= 2% session failures, cheap-model per-session and per-1k-exchange write cost, product-extract cache-read/write tokens and costs with and without cache reads, target-ability benefit and no regression

task13SharedEntity.protocol: Recorded from the same diagnostic leg: failures where the gold evidence shares an entity with a hit but no query term (counted from evidenceCounts and the term sets, no text).
task13SharedEntity.rule: >= 5% of a suite x model's failures -> reconsider typed links (owner gate); otherwise stays closed. No graph store is authorized.

maintainThenAnswer.rule: the only Task 5 arm that runs memory:maintain (once per history, before answering); every other arm runs without maintenance
maintainThenAnswer.scored: with the exchange exemption >= without it + 2 points on beam-100k/dev, and within 1 point of the no-maintain arm; offline: archived raw exchanges 29/293 and 73/94 -> 0, growth-stream month-1 active retrieval 0.5625 -> >= 0.9

weakHitsBelowFloor.variant: return the weak hits below the 0.34 relevance floor instead of 'no matching memory'
weakHitsBelowFloor.buildOnlyIf: the guidance leave-one-out (arm aggregation-loo) shows the floor causes the abstention gap: in some suite x model, >= 5% of the arm's abstention failures had the gold evidence among candidates below the floor (counted from evidenceCounts, no text)
weakHitsBelowFloor.ifBuilt: an opt-in tuning field, default off, measured once as a fix under fixKept; no second try

noTextRule: Reports and the decision record carry ids, labels, counts, rates and scores; never question, gold, note, claim or corpus text.
